messages:
Alex: Quick sync — Q3 roadmap decision needed for Dedicated: do we push burst-smoothing (tenant-level smoothing + carryover), quota visibility API, or the autoscale grace-window work first? Need a concrete prioritization + launch criteria by EOD.
Maria: My take: quota visibility API is high ROI for sales + CS. Customers keep asking for per-tenant live quota usage and historical spikes.
Jae: Agreed on visibility, but ops will drown if we surface quotas without guardrails. We need read-only views + rate limits on the quota API. Also need rollout plan for large customers.
Sam: From SRE: burst-smoothing impacts tail latency. If we do smoothing + carryover we must add observability for headroom + a canary that measures p95/p99 token latency and failed allocations. Otherwise we'll hurt SLAs.
Maria: Proposal: 1) quota visibility API (fast ship) 2) autoscale grace-window and preemption tweaks (medium) 3) burst-smoothing + carryover (medium/long, requires more validation).
Alex: That aligns with GTM ask. Can we detail launch criteria for #1 so eng can size?
Jae: Launch criteria for quota visibility API: 
- read-only per-tenant endpoints (no mutation)
- cached values with TTL 15s to avoid hot loops
- RBAC + token scope: `quota:read`
- export to Console and JSON endpoints for customers and CS
- metrics: request_latency, cache_hit_ratio, per-tenant_quota_percentile
- rollout: staged 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with rollback flag

Sam: Add SRE checks: alert if avg request latency > 300ms or cache_hit_ratio < 60% during rollout. Canary cluster should mimic 10% of production traffic.
Maria: Measurement for GTM: percent of CS requests closed without engineering involvement, time to answer quota questions in sales deck. We'll pilot with 3 customers.
product-bot: Created ticket RDW-1456 for "quota-visibility-api" and RDW-1457 for "autoscale-grace-window".
Alex: For autoscale grace-window (RDW-1457) quick spec: need a configurable delay (default 30s) before scaling down and an exponential backoff for scale-ups to avoid oscillation. Also allow per-pool overrides.
Sam: Sample config idea:
```yaml
autoscale:
  down_delay: 30s
  up_backoff_base: 10s
  max_scale_steps: 3
  per_pool_overrides: true
```
Jae: Important: persist recent allocation history in KV for the grace window; avoid relying only on ephemeral caches. That affects storage design.
Maria: Burst-smoothing doc: we should treat it as an economics feature — carryover credits vs latency budget. Big customers want predictable p95s, not burstiness. That means more telemetry and an opt-in trial.
Alex: Sounds like a plan. Action items: 
- Maria to own PM for quota-visibility (RDW-1456) and shepherd pilot.
- Jae to draft storage/rollout constraints and API contract by Tue.
- Sam to produce SRE rollout checklist + alert thresholds.
- Alex to sync with Sales + Solutions tomorrow 10a for pilot customers.
Maria: I'll start a short RFC and add the pilot criteria to the ticket.
Jae: I'll drop a short design note in RDW-1456 with the KV model and TTLs.
Sam: I'll add runbook stubs to RDW-1457 and RDW-1456.
Alex: If we can get the API + canary by end of Q2, we can convert pilot feedback into the autoscale and smoothing backlog for Q3. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Maria: One more thought — add a simple per-tenant "burst history" CSV export for enterprise customers. Low effort, high perceived value.
Alex: Good call, add to RDW-1456 scope as optional stretch.
product-bot: RDW-1456 assigned to Maria, RDW-1457 assigned to Engineering-Ops.
Alex: Closing thread — will follow up with a short prioritization doc in Confluence and a triage meeting invite.
